text.p: The neo-communist wife of Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic lambasted opposition protesters on Friday, accusing them in a magazine column of disrupting ordinary life and undermining the economy.
Mira Markovic wields considerable power behind the scenes as a key adviser to her husband and heads the Yugoslav United Left (JUL) party in Serbia's ruling leftist coalition.

Milosevic has ignored demands by the opposition Zajedno (Together) coalition for recognition of its victories in local elections annulled by his Socialist Party (SPS) on the grounds of unspecified "irregularities."

Markovic, whose contemptuous attitude towards dissent has made her the most despised figure in Serbia's ruling circle among opposition protesters, said Zajedno was interfering with the lives of countless people.

"Material damage has been constantly inflicted on the citizens of Belgrade who, because of two months of gatherings on the main streets, cannot use regular bus lines and are often forced to walk home in bitter cold," she wrote in her fortnightly column in the magazine Duga.
"Most business and personal contacts which should take place between midday and 6 p.m. in the centre of the city cannot take place now," said Markovic.
Markovic also claimed that Zajedno was being financed from abroad and accused Zajedno leaders, particularly populist Vuk Draskovic, of rhetoric that could provoke violent upheaval.

"Almost every day, from every gathering, threats of violence and death are made against the authorities not only unless they leave but also if they leave, and they must go so democracy can finally triumph in Serbia," she wrote.

"On the main evening news I heard Vuk Draskovic say from his platform that the entire leadership of JUL should be arrested ...The hooligans in Belgrade are threatening violence...in the name of democracy."
Draskovic has called for the arrest of JUL leaders if Zajedno rises to power in Serbia. But diplomats say he is often given to wild, crowd-pleasing oratory that should not always be taken seriously.
The opposition bloc has adhered strictly to non-violence but protesters have been sporadically attacked by riot police on the orders of hardline leftist security officials.
